name: The Hilltop Village
description: The historic core of Gordes, tiered stone houses climbing the hillside around the Renaissance castle and the Place du Château. Cobbled lanes, galleries, and restaurant terraces with sweeping Luberon views define the area, though summer brings heavy foot traffic and premium prices for anything within a short walk of the castle.
bestFor: Short stays, photographers, first-time visitors wanting the classic view
cons: Very touristy and crowded in summer
Limited parking and highest local prices

name: Les Imberts
description: A smaller settlement on the lower, flatter ground below the main village, along the road toward Cavaillon. Less picturesque than the hilltop but calmer, with easier parking, a couple of respected restaurants like Le Mas Tourteron, and more realistic day-to-day living for anyone renting nearby rather than staying purely for the postcard view.
bestFor: Longer stays, drivers wanting easier access and lower costs
cons: Still requires a car for everything

name: Senanque Abbey Valley
description: The valley just north of the village, home to the 12th-century Cistercian Abbaye de Sénanque and its famous lavender fields, which bloom from mid-June into July. A working monastery rather than a residential area, it draws heavy visitor traffic in bloom season via a single narrow access road, and is best appreciated on foot or by short drive rather than as a base.
bestFor: Day trips, photography, quiet reflection outside peak bloom
pros: Close to Gordes by short drive
cons: No accommodation or amenities on site

name: Roussillon
description: A striking Luberon village about 20 minutes east of Gordes, built into vivid red and orange ochre cliffs with an ochre trail (Sentier des Ocres) walk just outside town. It offers a similar hilltop-village charm with its own distinct color palette, more affordable dining than Gordes, and makes a natural day trip or alternate base for anyone touring the Luberon.
bestFor: Day trips, alternate basing for Luberon exploration
